title: The turn, closed

lines: A LOOK BACK DOWN THE ROAD.
cards: A wagon stops at the side of the road, with room still on board. For three weeks this path has been riding in one: Mahayana, the great vehicle.
A vehicle is something that carries, and this name says the carrying is meant for everyone standing at the side of the road.
The bodhisattva, the perfections, Buddha-nature, Buddhas in every direction, the great beings with their swords and vows. Today the wagon stops for a moment, so you can look back down the road.

teach.h: A NAME, AND AN OPEN QUESTION.
teach.b: First, the name and the start. Mahayana, the name this movement gave itself. You met the courtesy that goes with it: call each school by its own name, Theravada for Theravada.
And an honest gap: how it began is still debated, and nobody has settled it.
Second, the one who carries others. The bodhisattva, who seeks awakening for the sake of all. The six perfections: giving, ethics, patience, effort, meditation, wisdom.
The ten grounds, the first one called joy. Under all of it, Buddha-nature, covered but never lost, even in a difficult person. Third, a crowded sky.
Countless Buddhas in countless worlds. Avalokiteshvara, the one who hears the cries of the world. Manjushri, whose sword cuts through confusion.
Samantabhadra and his great vows. Maitreya, the one to come, honored in Theravada too. Ksitigarbha, who goes to the lowest places.
And skillful means, the teaching shaped to whoever is listening.
Fourth, the book and the vow. The perfection of wisdom, from long sutras down to a single letter, honored as the mother of the Buddhas.
The four great vows. Dedication, the good of practice given away. The book honored with flowers.
And two views of the Buddha's word, held side by side. Put it all together and one shape shows through: the turn this block traced is a turn outward. Practice isn't only for the one practicing.
The vehicle is wide on purpose. Tomorrow the path opens the Diamond Sutra, on an ordinary morning.

how: Mahayana Buddhism is practiced across East Asia, Tibet, the Himalayas and beyond, where people take bodhisattva vows, chant sutras, and honor bodhisattvas such as Guanyin, Manjushri and Ksitigarbha.

o: the moment a monk turns back toward ordinary life
the Mahayana turn outward: a path wide enough for all beings
a turning of the prayer wheel at the end of a practice

games.q: the great vehicle: tap the pairs.

s: Mahayana is the name the movement gave itself
the great vehicle; and each school is called by its own name, Theravada for Theravada.
scholars have settled exactly how Mahayana began
how it began is still debated.
Buddha-nature can be lost in a difficult person
covered, the teaching says, but never lost.

games.q: you've spent three weeks on the Mahayana turn. which way does the turn point?
games.why: outward. the bodhisattva seeks awakening for the sake of all, and even the merit of practice is given away.

practice: Let the four vows come back on four out-breaths, numberless, endless, beyond measure, nothing above it, in your community's words if you chant them.
Then let the words go and simply sit, like a wide wagon at the side of the road with room still on board. When a face or a worry comes, let it climb on; there's room.

wordCard.voice: The turn. The Mahayana turn outward: bodhisattvas, perfections, Buddha-nature, many Buddhas, a path wide enough for all beings. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the great vehicle, the name this movement gave itself.

carryVoice: Your line: the great vehicle. There's always room for one more on board. Three weeks, done.
